sol.section: Recommended exact spec changes (§12.3), Exclusion evidence and default validation, final artifact-delivery paragraph
sol.problem: The claim that artifact delivery can use 'existing certificate attachments' is false. ISA 0.9 §9.1 enumerates a closed object/metadata schema and makes unknown sections or fields errors; §12.3 defines no attachments field or transport. The proposal introduces a replay obligation but attributes its delivery mechanism to an existing contract that does not supply it. This is a false existing-coverage premise under convergence rule 1, rather than a request for field-level encoding completeness.
sol.fix: Replace that paragraph with: 'ISA 0.9 defines no certificate-attachment transport. This repair introduces a separate checker input bundle containing the certificate and the required content-addressed artifacts. By default, classifier and input-map blobs are supplied outside the ISA object and certificate schemas; artifact_hash and input_map_hash are SHA-256 of their exact raw bytes. The checker verifies those digests before replay. Missing required blobs make the exclusion report unchecked; mismatched digests reject it. Other transports MAY supply the identical addressed bytes.' Existing materialisation, program, native-build and domain binding obligations still apply. Alternatively, explicitly introduce a new certificate attachments member and its default interpretation in §§9.1/12.3; I recommend the external bundle because it avoids another metadata extension. For the synthetic fixture, valid supplied artifacts reproduce undefined_excluded="64"; absent artifacts leave that exclusion report unchecked while the independent F_B recount may still verify faults_by_code={"1":"256"}.
